analysis.answer_text: Okay, let’s walk through a quick troubleshooting routine together to steady that connection.First, move closer to the router and watch the Wi-Fi icon to see if the signal becomes stable; if it does, interference or range might be the issue. Next,
analysis.reply_text: First, move closer to the router so we’re not fighting a weak signal, and if you can, set your device on a stable surface to keep it from switching networks. Next, toggle Wi-Fi off, wait about ten seconds, and turn it back on to reset the connection. Then, forget the network in your Wi-Fi settings, reconnect, and re-enter the password to clear out any bad saved configuration. After that, restart your router and modem by unplugging them for about thirty seconds, then plugging them back in and waiting for the lights to stabilize. Next, check for interference: turn off or move away from other wireless devices like baby monitors or cordless phones, and avoid metal objects blocking the router. Finally, update your device’s Wi-Fi driver or operating system, and if it still drops, log into the router’s admin page and switch to a less crowded channel or try the 5 gigahertz band.
